issues.description: Inconsistent method naming for the developer experience description: the problem statement and the template expect an instance method named swiftExperienceDescription(), but the solution's Developer.swift defines the method as getExperienceDescription(). The solution's Client.swift still calls swiftExperienceDescription(), producing a mismatch between the class API and its usage. This inconsistency can cause confusion and may lead to compilation errors or incorrect references when students compare template, spec, and reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription() and update the initializer to call swiftExperienceDescription(), or (B) change the template and problem text to use getExperienceDescription() and update Client.swift to call getExperienceDescription(). Ensure the same method name is used in the problem statement, template, solution implementation, and client usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an instance method named swiftExperienceDescription() on Developer, but the solution implementation defines the equivalent method as getExperienceDescription(). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (producing a developer Swift experience description) creates a mapping confusion: students will look for swiftExperienceDescription() (as described in the instructions and present in the template) but see a different name in the solution. The solution's Client also calls swiftExperienceDescription(), which mismatches the solution Developer implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution method getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription() and update the initializer to call swiftExperienceDescription(), so the problem statement, template, client usage, and solution implementation all use the same identifier.
